correctness.rationale: The operator has one root with d≥2 outgoing infinite rays, positive root weights a_i and constant positive tail weights c_i, and fixed 0<t<1. Distinct input columns have disjoint images, so |S_m| is diagonal and the polar recursion is exactly a_{i,m+1}=a_{i,m}c_i^t R_m^{-t/2}, while all tail weights remain c_i. Normalized squared root weights follow softmax ratios proportional to a_i²(c_i/C)^{2tm}; their log-normalization z_m tends to zero as Q rho^{2m}, with rho=max_{c_i<C}(c_i/C)^t and Q the total leading normalized slow mass. The remaining root-column logarithm satisfies h_{m+1}=(1-t)h_m+z_{m+1}-z_m, whence h_m→0. Since all nonroot columns agree throughout, the squared operator-norm error is exactly C²{[e^{(h_m-z_m)/2}-1]^2+e^{h_m}(1-e^{-z_m})}. Comparing the scalar eta=1-t mode with the slow-ray rho mode yields precisely the four nonzero limits, including the quadrature constant at eta=rho and the cancellation H=0 when eta>rho. The series H converges for eta≥rho because the forcing decays as rho^{2m}; root rescaling changes H by 2log(s) without changing rho,Q. The all-equal-tail boundary reduces to a scalar exponential. An independent 35-iterate four-regime recurrence comparison passed; its finite nature is explicitly distinguished from norm-convergence proof.
residual_risks: Finite numerical/modular experiments corroborate but do not substitute for analytic or integer-exact proofs.
